One row = 3 ints = 12 bytes.

- x + 3 = address of row 3 = 2000 + 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 12 = 2036
- *(x + 3) = address of x[3][0] = 2036
- *(x + 2) + 3 = address of x[2][0] + 3 ints = 2024 + 12 = 2036

Answer: 2036, 2036, 2036

questions.text: The graph shown below has 8 edges with distinct integer edge weights. The minimum spanning tree (MST) is of weight 36 and contains the edges: {(A, C), (B, C), (B, E), (E, F), (D, F)}. The edge weights of only those edges which are in the MST are given in the figure shown below. The minimum possible sum of weights of all 8 edges of this graph is ___________.
questions.solution:
MST weights: AC = 9, BC = 2, BE = 15, EF = 4, DF = 6 (total 36). A non-MST edge must be heavier than every MST edge on its cycle (weights are distinct).

- AB: cycle A-C-B, max 9 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] AB [latex]\ge[/latex] 10
- CD: path C-B-E-F-D, max 15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CD [latex]\ge[/latex] 16
- DE: path D-F-E, max 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] DE [latex]\ge[/latex] 7

Minimum total = 36 + 10 + 16 + 7 = 69

Answer: 69

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

For each of the n iterations:
- the j loop makes [latex]p\approx\log n[/latex]
- the k loop doubles k up to p, adding [latex]\log p\approx\log\log n[/latex] to q

q [latex]\approx n\log\log n[/latex]

Answer: [latex]n\log(\log n)[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the following pseudo code, where x and y are positive integers. 
 begin
   q := 0
    r := x 
    while r >= y  do
         begin
               r := r - y
              q := q + 1
        end
end
The post condition that needs to be satisfied after the program terminates is
questions.solution:
The loop subtracts y from r and counts it in q, which is division of x by y. Invariant: x = qy + r. The loop stops when r [latex]\lt[/latex] y.

Answer: {x = qy + r [latex]\wedge[/latex] r [latex]\lt[/latex] y}
